meta.name: Simmons-style live game one-liners: golden set (Adam, Oct 4)
meta.constraint: Every line describes a game that is still being played (early, middle, or late). No line implies a final result.
meta.note: Illustrative voice anchors, not payloads: game_state is a summary, so these cannot be replayed through the writer. Some lines invent facts on purpose (owners, boosters, crowds).

examples.line: Two offenses trying to outpunt each other is the NFL's version of a staring contest.
The offensive coordinator just called a draw play on 3rd-and-15 and somehow that's not even the worst thing that happened this drive.
The only suspense left is whether the losing team's owner is watching from a box or hiding in a bathroom.

examples.situation: Backup QB in and playing well
examples.line: The backup is 8-for-9 and now every fan is quietly planning a quarterback controversy.

examples.situation: Home leads by 7, opponent has the ball
examples.line: This is the exact moment every lead in the NFL stops being a lead and becomes an anxiety disorder.
This is a decision your coach will be remembered for in either direction, forever, on podcasts.

examples.situation: Home kicked a field goal on the first OT possession; the other team now has the ball
examples.line: The league's overtime rules have once again produced the most dramatic coin flip in American sports.
The final score of this game is going to look like a baseball result and feel like a root canal.

examples.situation: Both teams losing starters to injury
examples.line: Both teams are down so many starters that the broadcast just started naming guys like a witness protection list.
Garbage time is when I learn the names of seven guys I'll forget by Tuesday.
The first quarter of this game is a crime scene with a marching band.

examples.situation: Unranked home team leading a top-10 opponent; upset brewing
examples.line: The underdog is playing with the confidence of a team that has nothing to lose and a booster who just promised a car.
Rivalry games are the only place where a 10-10 slugfest feels like a duel.

examples.situation: Home going for it on 4th-and-short, crowd roaring
examples.line: College football is dumb and beautiful, and right now the sound is shaking a stadium of people who will remember this forever.
Nobody in the building has a pulse that makes sense.

examples.situation: QB scrambling, forces a throw, turnover
examples.line: That's the kind of throw you only see when a 20-year-old thinks his career depends on it.
The play-calling has gone from aggressive to the coach running his own SAT prep.

examples.situation: Home trailed by 24 at half, comeback building
examples.line: Down 24 at half was a lot, but this crowd is making it sound like a revival.

examples.situation: Heavy underdog at home leads late; students edging toward the rail
examples.line: The student section has already picked its landing spot on the field, and security has clearly noticed.

examples.situation: Home returns a kick for a touchdown
examples.line: The special teams unit just scored for a coach who barely watches them practice.
Both teams are scoring like the other side's defense is a rumor.

examples.situation: Star has hit five straight threes
examples.line: That's not a shooting night, that's a mood.
Nobody played defense, nobody wanted to, and the over is already sweating.
A 20-0 run is the NBA's way of saying thanks for coming, now please go home.
The next two minutes are going to have more hero ball than a Marvel marathon.
The whole building knows who's getting the ball, the defense knows it too, and it's still going to be a sin.

examples.situation: Home star at the free-throw line
examples.line: Free throws in crunch time are the loneliest thing in sports, and nobody talks about it enough.

examples.situation: Deep bench player on a heater
examples.line: The 12th man is heating up and the coach looks like a parent who forgot to pick him up.

examples.situation: Blowout, home crowd heading for the exits
examples.line: When the crowd starts leaving with 7 minutes left, you're watching an obituary with sneakers.
Everyone's legs are gone, the three-pointers are floating like prayers, and I love it.

examples.situation: Red card to the away side
examples.line: A red card in the first twenty minutes means ninety minutes of suffering for one team and a very long evening for the other.
Forty-five minutes of football so tidy that we're all begging for a mistake.
That break is so clean it should come with a signature.
The late equalizer is the most English kind of heartbreak: well-earned, brutal, and followed by someone screaming at a corner flag.

examples.situation: Stoppage time, home side crossing it into the box
examples.line: Stoppage time, 1-1, and one more cross decides whether we get a lifetime of dinner stories or a lifetime of therapy.

examples.situation: Home fans booing their own team
examples.line: The home crowd just discovered that booing is a team sport.

examples.situation: VAR check on a disallowed goal
examples.line: The ball crossed the line, a man in a room disagreed, and now everyone is reading a ruling like it's scripture.
This is a game where every tackle feels like a hostage negotiation.

examples.situation: Leading side wasting time at goal kicks
examples.line: Seeing a team take eleven seconds to take a goal kick is the purest form of football gamesmanship.
Derbies don't have a halftime, they have a cease-fire.

examples.situation: Early goal before fans are settled
examples.line: The goal came so early the stadium is still looking for its seats.
This is a perfectly fine soccer game that will be completely forgotten by Wednesday, which is also what makes MLS charming.
A two-goal lead in MLS is a polite suggestion.

examples.situation: Late red card, home player sent off
examples.line: The ref just removed a man with five minutes left, and the stadium reacted like he'd cancelled the playoffs.

examples.situation: Final corner kick of stoppage time
examples.line: Last corner of the night, 1-1, and the entire stadium has forgotten the schedule, the travel, and the rule book.
The marquee signing has touched the ball 11 times and somehow still seems tired.
The only thing louder than the goal chant is the one guy who still thinks he's here for the beer.
Penalty shootouts are the only moment in sports when everyone is a coward and a hero simultaneously.

examples.situation: Lightning delay, players off the pitch
examples.line: The lightning delay gives this game a real sports-as-soap-opera feel.
Both teams are playing out the string like it's a teacher's last day before summer.
